problem: Prior visual object navigation work focuses on better feature embeddings (object distributions, graph representations), which do not effectively handle partially-known environments and obstacles, since a single policy conflates going toward the target with obstacle avoidance and exploration.
motivation: Navigation in complex environments requires alternating between goal-directed movement and local obstacle avoidance/exploration. Treating all hidden states uniformly ignores these differing objectives, so separating and rewarding them separately should help.
key_idea: Classify hidden states by current navigation objective (long-term: approach the target; short-term: avoid obstacles and explore), reward them separately, and combine reweighted past states via a state memory with an adjustment gate and an action-boosting gate.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that separating objectives and handling their alternation via memory gating matters more than better feature embeddings alone.
method: Long-short objective policy: hidden states are classified by the current navigation objective and separately rewarded.
Long-term objective: move closer to the target object.
Short-term objective: obstacle avoidance and exploration.
State memory with adjustment gate: stores states and mitigates the effect of alternation between long- and short-term objectives.
Action-boosting gate: reweights and combines all past hidden states for action prediction.

setting.backbone: Recurrent policy network with state memory and gates (details not given in abstract)
